title: Two of Everything in Berlin - Quick Summary
items: **Berlin has two of almost everything because each half of the divided city built its own.** Two zoos, two opera houses, two concert halls, two planetariums, two state library buildings, two city halls, two universities, two museum quarters, and for forty years two main stations and two airport systems.

**The centre you came for is the eastern half.** Museum Island, the Staatsoper, the Konzerthaus, the Fernsehturm and the Rotes Rathaus all sit within about fifteen minutes of each other in East Berlin, which is why almost every walking tour of Berlin starts there.

**The western twins are the ones nobody tells you about, and two of them are genuinely worth the trip.** The **Funkturm** at the Messe grounds has a 126 m platform open Tuesday to Sunday, 11:00 to 21:00, and almost no queue. **Rathaus Schoeneberg** rings its Freedom Bell at **noon** from the balcony where Kennedy spoke in 1963.

**Some pairs were settled by the reunified city and you no longer get a choice.** Bahnhof Zoo and Ostbahnhof both lost their long-distance trains when Berlin Hauptbahnhof opened in May 2006. Tegel closed in 2020, Tempelhof in 2008, and the eastern airport at Schoenefeld became BER.

**Pick one side per day, not one of each.** A Museum Island morning and a Charlottenburg afternoon is two U-Bahn crossings and a lost hour. The tool below plots both halves of every pair on a real map so you can see how far your day is actually spread.
